focus.name: focus-on-spot
focus.purpose: Inside the blue task band (.on-spot); white rings were invisible on white buttons on blue.

focus.name: hint-ring
focus.purpose: Hint level 3 on cards; pulses in Full motion, static when Off.

motion.name: modes
motion.purpose: Calm removes tilt, parallax and flips (crossfade instead); Off zeroes all durations. Every animation has a screen-reader text twin.

cardLayer.materials: Gilt (yours) or moon-silver (opponent) conic frame, dark navy face with noise, foil and glare, parallax art, rounded 6cqw corners, drop shadow.

narrative.overview:
The lesson reads like a quick-start rules sheet from a game box. Each step is a numbered panel framed in ink; the board is that panel's diagram, drawn on ruled paper with a "Fig." caption, lettered pins and a printed red arrow. The learner reads one bold task, looks at the diagram, taps, and gets a one-line correction tied to the card it concerns.

The sheet is flat, cool white and ink. Two spot inks do all the signalling: blue for the task and for selection, red only for mistakes. A highlighter yellow marks what to look at. Density is low and type is large; Lexend carries all UI text because it reads easily for learners with dyslexia. The world refuses both the dark fantasy glow of the game's own marketing and the soft, rounded white edtech app.

The collectible cards are a separate, preserved layer: they keep their original dark, gilt-framed, foil-and-parallax design and their own fonts and inks. The sheet frames them; it never restyles them.
keyCharacteristics: Cool white sheet, white panels, 3px ink frame rules, square corners.
One spot blue for task, current step and selection; red only for mistakes, life and the attack arrow.
Highlighter yellow for callouts, hints and selected text.
Board drawn on ruled paper with a Fig. caption, lettered pins and a Key.
Every state is an icon plus a word, never color alone.
Flat: no gradients as fills, no glow, no blur, no glass in UI chrome.

rules.name: The Two Spot Inks Rule
rules.body: Blue means "the task / your choice"; red means "a mistake / damage". Red never decorates, never marks a creature as a target, and never stands in for blue.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Yellow is for callouts, hints and selected text. Its one other use is accessibility: the keyboard focus ring on the blue task band is yellow, because a white ring on white buttons on blue was invisible.

rules.name: The Icon-Plus-Word Rule
rules.body: Every state pairs a shape (icon, badge, ring, check) with a word. Color confirms; it never carries meaning alone.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: All UI text is Lexend. Card fonts stay inside cards.

rules.name: The Short Line Rule
rules.body: Prompts are one bold line of at most 8 words; feedback is one line led by a bold tone word.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: No gradients as fills, no glow, no blur, no glass in UI chrome. The board's ruled lines are hard-stop lines, not a gradient fill.

dos: **Do** frame every step as one white panel with a 3px ink rule, and separate its regions with 3px ink rules.
**Do** use spot blue for the task band, the current step and selection only.
**Do** keep red for mistakes, life hearts and the printed attack arrow, and point the arrow at the opponent's life column.
**Do** lead feedback with a round icon badge and a bold tone word (Right / Not quite / Note) on a tinted fill.
**Do** use the yellow focus ring (with a blue gap) for anything focusable on the blue task band; the blue two-tone ring everywhere else.
**Do** label board marks with lettered pins and explain them in a Key.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or more and buttons at 48px.
**Do** put actions, feedback and the Key directly under the board on phones.
donts: **Don't** round UI chrome corners; circles are only for pins, discs and badges.
**Don't** use gradients as fills, glow, blur or glass in the UI.
**Don't** mark feedback with a colored side stripe.
**Don't** point the attack arrow at a creature.
**Don't** set UI text in the card fonts, or restyle the card faces with UI tokens.
**Don't** show a state with color alone.
